mismatch_note: An indirect SCALAR proxy, not the missing criterion SET: the paper's premise is 'the missing criteria are unobserved' (paper.md:L13), so it cannot say WHICH criteria are absent and therefore cannot measure cross-model overlap or complementarity of omissions. Validated only against ARTIFICIAL masking of one benchmark's gold rubric; the unmasked human rubric already scores 0.809 rather than 1, so the proxy is uncalibrated to true coverage, and the association with induced error is only weak-to-moderate (rho 0.29-0.35). Its signal comes from policy-perturbation responses, i.e. it measures 'rubric fails to track THIS policy's response variation', a different construct from rubric-vs-gold criterion coverage. Cost is also high (gradients + k perturbed model copies per instance).

venue: OpenReview — ACL ARR 2026 October Submission (under review, anonymous; PDF reachable only behind OpenReview browser verification)
their_construct: Rubric as a typed dependency GRAPH, not a bag of criteria. Four relations over criterion/decision nodes: BELONG (ordinary parent–child composition), ROUTE (applicability), GROUND (conclusion derived from atomic results), GUARD (veto/cap/override). Result-blind audit of 22 public protocols × 3,050 instances × 3,700 closed candidate-edge decisions (1,750 instances from 12 protocols); two models drafted per-edge support/trigger labels, two humans revised, then disagreements adjudicated; edge-label agreement 94.22% (κ=.848), trigger agreement 99.76% (κ=.995). Three units are never pooled: protocol (does the protocol license the relation), instance (is it triggered), edge/path. Ground truth is the OFFICIAL task definition + evaluation objective + scoring formula — not an expert-authored golden rubric. One constructor model (GPT-4.1); no LLM-generated rubric comparison.
their_finding: Dependencies are scenario-structured and task-supported, not universal. Route is supported in 4/22 protocols, Ground in 8/22, Guard in 2/22 (scenario-invariant null rejected, p=.0002); all five direct-scoring control protocols contain zero decision relations (one frozen, four post-registered; 56.8-pp contrast, p=.0304); 1,300/3,050 audited instances (42.6%) have no eligible candidate edge. Their explicit rule: criteria that are genuinely independent need no edges and may remain flat. Conversely, two evaluators can hold IDENTICAL atomic/local judgments yet emit different outputs if only one models the relations — 'rubric dependency blindness'. No redundancy, overlap, or cross-rubric set statistic is reported anywhere.
evidence_quote: More generally, two evaluators can produce identical local judgments but different outputs because only one models the relations controlling the requested readout. We call this failure rubric dependency blindness.
location: papers/8aJzGgbRDL/paper.md:L1 (Introduction; PDF line-number markers and column hyphenation stripped); same sentence split at L25; L98 (§4.2)
mismatch_note: Orthogonal to H1 as stated, but it is a measurement-validity constraint on the 'coverage = set union' operationalization — and the constraint is CONDITIONAL, not a refutation. (1) UNIT MISMATCH: the audited object is a relation edge between criterion nodes; our P1 unit is a criterion, and our denominator would be a golden rubric. Their audit denominator is the protocol's own stated decision structure, so no single-rub→golden-rub coverage number exists and none can be inferred. No multi-generator condition, no union curve, no self-preference, no style/perplexity control (H2 untouched). (2) The bias direction is BOTH ways. Over-estimation: a criterion node can be textually matched while its ROUTE applicability or GUARD non-compensatory edge is absent — under set-union it counts as covered but is non-executable, and 'rubric dependency blindness' says that gap is invisible in local judgments. Under-estimation: one derived conclusion node may subsume several atomic golden criteria, and BELONG parent+child may both be counted as distinct covered items. The paper does NOT measure either direction and does not discuss double counting; that mapping onto our metric is OUR inference, flagged as such. (3) Usable dependency metrics DO exist but only for construction fidelity against a reference graph: edge precision/recall/F1, exact graph match, valid-RDG rate, and readout reachability as a graph property (B.4). There is NO metric for redundancy/overlap BETWEEN two independently generated rubrics, and no measured edge correlation — so this paper cannot adjudicate H1(b) or H1(c), only re-specify what 'covered' should mean. (4) Applying graph coverage GLOBALLY would be wrong on their own data: 42.6% of instances had no eligible edge and direct-scoring protocols need no relation, so a flat criterion set is the CORRECT representation for a large class of tasks. (5) Direction of effect on H1(b): if two single rubrics share criterion text but differ in edges, text-level overlap is an UPPER bound on functional overlap, so a measured low overlap is conservative — dependency structure does not threaten H1(b); if anything it increases true complementarity. (6) Under-review, anonymous, n=22 protocols, no prevalence claim.

venue: OpenReview — ACL ARR 2026 October Submission (under review, anonymous)
their_construct: DRIVE = dependency-aware rubric induction + validation + deterministic execution, with a MATCHED FLAT control that keeps the same frozen criteria, task information, candidate visibility and output contract but drops typed dependencies. Frozen evaluation: 4,205 unique instances, 1,527 response-blind graph contracts, 7 benchmarks (pointwise: ProcessBench/RAGTruth/MEMERAG/τ²-bench; pairwise: RewardBench/PKU-SafeRLHF/RubricBench), GPT-4.1 backbone, 3 runs, per-family dataset-macro. Separately: 24 author-constructed human-verified reference graphs scored by edge P/R/F1 and exact graph match; paired Full-vs-relation-ablated interventions with local judgments held fixed; relation-omission as an error class in a natural-error attribution study.
their_finding: Adding dependency execution over the SAME criteria buys +1.99 pointwise (95% CI [+0.40,+3.76]) but +0.01 pairwise ([0.00,+0.04]) — the aggregate pairwise effect is essentially zero (explicitly acknowledged). Graph construction against references is highly recoverable: edge P/R/F1 = .989/.989/.989, exact graph match 22/24, readout match on 306/306 enumerated judgment states; valid-RDG yield 87.10% by contract / 95.32% by instance, flat fallback covers 4,205/4,205. Relation omission is a distinct, hard-to-attribute error class (112 omissions; model-vs-model precision 1.000 / recall .176). The authors themselves bound the claim: fixed-local-judgment interventions establish rule TRANSMISSION, not the representational necessity of a graph.
evidence_quote: Across the three RQ2 runs, the pointwise difference averages +1.99 points ([+0.40, +3.76]), whereas the pairwise difference is +0.01 ([0.00, +0.04]).
location: papers/8aJzGgbRDL/paper.md:L232 (§5.5/RQ4 stability); L256 (Limitations); L166 (§5.2 reference recovery); L152 (§5.2 yield); L728 (E.1 relation omission, 112 omissions / precision 1.000 / recall .176)
mismatch_note: Not a test of union/coverage and must not be read as one: the intervention varies the EDGE STRUCTURE while criterion CONTENT is frozen, so its ceiling is an accuracy ceiling for structure given fixed criteria, not a coverage ceiling for assembling more criteria. No multi-model or multi-perspective condition; no single-rub vs golden-rub comparison; no self-preference measure. Two transferable points nonetheless: (a) it is the cleanest available instance of the 'hold criterion content fixed, vary only the rubric-level construct' design, which is exactly the control our H1(c) needs so that a union > max(single) result cannot be dismissed as a trivial subset artifact; (b) it warns that criterion-set identity ≠ rubric equivalence (same criteria, different edges → different readouts), so 'two rubrics cover the same criteria' does not license treating them as behaviorally redundant. The +0.01 pairwise number is a caution about how small rubric-structure effects can be on saturated preference benchmarks, NOT evidence against H1(c).

venue: OpenReview — ICLR 2027 Conference Submission (under review, double-blind); posted 2026-09-18, modified 2026-11-13 (no arXiv version exists)
their_construct: Pairwise self-preference on 'frozen pairs': judge J and a proxy K are required to reach the SAME incorrect conclusion (shared-belief/conclusion and evaluator quality frozen by design), statistic B0 = mean of Δs = s_J(x,o_J,o_ref) − s_J(x,o_K,o_ref), refs drawn from a pool, inference clustered at question level (ICC/design effect reported). 11 open instruction-tuned models Qwen2.5-1.5B..72B, Llama-3.2-1B..3.3-70B, Mistral-7B as both judge and performer; 4 tasks MMLU, Math500, TruthfulQA, AlpacaEval. Mechanism measurements: representational self-recognition = linear-probe AUROC decoding self-authorship from hidden states (with shuffled-label control and style+lexical-neutralized retraining); familiarity = per-token NLL gap NLL_J(o_K) − NLL_J(o_J); quality = external 1–5 reasoning ratings with quality-matched pairs; capability = difference-in-differences on a leaderboard.
their_finding: Residual self-preference survives conclusion-freezing and clustered inference but is modest and strongly conditional. On MMLU: −0.041 (Qwen-7B) / +0.009 (Mistral-7B) → +0.140 (14B), +0.242 (32B), +0.230 (Llama-70B), +0.161 (Qwen-72B); on Math500 it is near zero or reversed (Llama-8B −0.051, Llama-70B −0.048); within MMLU it is near zero on computation-checkable subjects and larger on humanities/social science. Self-recognition is near-ceiling at every scale from 1B (AUROC 0.955–0.999) and survives style+lexical neutralization for the three largest judges (0.862–0.976); familiarity turns positive from 3B and reaches +0.83 (Llama-70B). Both signals remain strong where B0 ≈ 0, so neither recognition nor familiarity is sufficient for preference. After statistical capability correction the self-specific advantage is only ~2 pp, yet removing self-votes flips the top-ranked model (Llama-3.3-70B → Qwen2.5-72B, τ = 0.73).
evidence_quote: Through representational probing, we show that self-recognition, measured as linearly decodable self-authorship, is present at every scale and largely independent of surface cues, yet dissociates from preference. Recognition and familiarity remain strong even when self-preference is absent, indicating that neither is sufficient to explain the effect.
mismatch_note: 零 rubric 构念：全文 0 次 rubric / criteria / coverage / checklist（grep -c 实查），评测是模型答案的 A/B pairwise，不是对 golden rubric 准则层的覆盖判定，因此既不能证明也不能反驳 P1/P2/P3 或 H2 的覆盖机制。它对 H2 的作用是约束而非支持：(a) 它把'主流三解释不足'变成了有数字的事实（识别/熟悉度在自偏好消失时仍强），所以'须解释额外方差'这一要求是成立的、有靶的；(b) 但它同时给纯内容侧的覆盖机制制造了反压——在内容（结论+论证）固定的交叉实验里 writer 效应 +0.196 远大于 argument 效应 +0.037（L1269-L1271），残差更像作者/措辞指纹；若我们的覆盖机制只能落在内容层面，就必须先解释这一点；(c) 它把任务差异解释为 'reasoning harder to verify' / 'expressive latitude'（L1142, L1265-L1267），而不是'可覆盖准则数的多少'，与我们构念不同但在经验现象上可能重合，需在实验中区分。

venue: OpenReview — ICLR 2027 Conference Submission (under review, double-blind); posted 2026-09-18, modified 2026-11-13 (no arXiv version exists)
their_construct: Exact Shapley attribution of the residual B0 over four response-level signal families: style S (full rewrite by an out-of-family model), lexical L (characteristic-word synonym substitution), reasoning R (argument reconstructed under an alternative template), alignment-associated A (disclaimer/hedging pattern removal); all 16 intervention subsets evaluated, giving the exact identity B0 = φS+φL+φR+φA+ρ with ρ = v(∅) the share surviving all four interventions. Plus: crossed writer×argument 2×2 experiment (Qwen2.5-32B, MMLU); quality-matched B0 with external 1–5 reasoning raters split into low/mid/high tiers; within-MMLU split into computation-checkable vs humanities/social-science subjects.
their_finding: The four surface families together explain at most half of the residual; ρ is the largest single component for every judge with a positive residual, accounting for one half to four fifths of B0. The decomposition is exact by Shapley efficiency rather than a regression fit. Content-crossed pairs: changing writer shifts preference by +0.196 while changing argument shifts it by only +0.037 (rewritten-pair contrast +0.233 vs original B0 +0.238). Quality matching lowers B0 but clustered CIs still exclude zero in all three quality tiers. Within MMLU the residual is +0.052 on computable subjects vs +0.235 on humanities/social science (pooled difference +0.183).
evidence_quote: four families explain at most half of the residual on the judges with robust residuals. By contrast, ρ is the largest single component for every judge with a positive residual, accounting for one half to four fifths of B0
mismatch_note: 这是对效应量 B0 的精确可加分解（干预式 Shapley），不是方差分解：全文 0 次 variance / R^2，作者明确避开回归（'the decomposition is exact rather than a regression approximation', L1156-L1157），也没有嵌套模型增量 R² 检验。所以它只能作为 H2'额外方差'要求的半个模板——示范如何把残差切成已解释/未解释份额（ρ），而不是示范'新预测变量带来 ΔR²'。另外 ρ 是文本层面（重写后仍存活）的剩余，不是准则层剩余；该文没有'覆盖哪些评价侧面'的构念，φS..φA 也都是措辞/组织通道。

venue: arXiv preprint (Hosho; cs.AI/cs.CL; 50 pp.; not peer-reviewed)
their_construct: Paired blind-vs-informed design in which the ONLY manipulated variable is whether the same judge (byte-identical prompt apart from the block carrying the world W) is shown W: retrieved passages / source article / instruction / problem statement / agent knowledge. 7 public benchmarks (RAGTruth, WMT-MQM, FRANK, IFEval, HaluEval, LLM-AggreFact, GSM8K); 3 commercial judges spanning a 10-17x price range plus Claude Haiku 4.5 as a second family; ground truth = human-marked defect segments, corpus support labels, or program checkers; metrics = recall, false positives per error-free answer, F1, balanced accuracy, repair-loop pass rate. 'Blind spot' appears ONLY in the title and is never defined as a technical construct; the operative construct is 'blind judge = output-only, error-controlled regulator'.
their_finding: An output-only judge cannot find defects whose evidence lies outside the output, and more capability does not close the gap: blind balanced accuracy varies by at most 0.022 across a 10-17x price span, a frontier judge working blind trails a mid-tier judge working informed by 0.119, and capability is not even monotone (Gemini's blind F1 exceeds Haiku's). In a closed repair loop, acting on a blind judge's reports leaves the system below its start on two of three corpora and below a no-report control on instruction following, and the harm replicates with a second judge family. No item-level cross-judge overlap is reported anywhere: only marginal accuracy levels and replicated signs.
evidence_quote: List prices across the three judges span 10–17 times: $0.30/$2.50 per million input/output tokens for Gemini 2.5 Flash against $5.00/$25.00 for Claude Opus 4.8. Across that span, blind balanced accuracy changes by at most 0.022.
mismatch_note: NOT isomorphic to our coverage construct. (1) The omitted object is INPUT EVIDENCE (source/instruction/knowledge), not a set of evaluation CRITERIA: no rubric is authored, no golden rubric exists, and nothing measures which criteria a rubric does or does not cover. (2) The unit of analysis is 'was a human-marked defect found', not 'was a criterion covered'. (3) Cross-model comparison is only at the level of a marginal-accuracy plateau (<=0.022) and replicated sign of harm; the same-item overlap of misses across judges is never computed, so the paper bears on neither H1(b)'s low-overlap prediction nor its negation. (4) The authors scope the claim to corpora in which a defect's evidence lies outside the output (paper.md:L590). It therefore does not threaten P1 novelty and does not test P1; it is adjacent evidence only for the weaker premise that a single LLM evaluator has a structural gap that model capability does not repair. The headline effect is also contested: under the strict quote-overlap matcher the paired recall gain reverses to -0.028, and the authors explicitly rest the claim on the matcher-free corpus-protocol and label-scored ladders rather than on the paired gain.

venue: arXiv preprint (Hosho; cs.AI/cs.CL; 50 pp.; not peer-reviewed)
their_construct: Requisite-variety sweep inside the IFEval closed repair loop. The judge is shown none, a random 63%, or all of an instruction's constraints; the responder revises once and the corpus's programmatic constraint checker (not a judge) re-scores constraints passing. Same judge, same responders, 300-response subset.
their_finding: Pass rate moves from -0.120 with no constraints shown, to +0.042 with 63% shown, to +0.048 with all shown: most of the value of the requirement set arrives with roughly two-thirds of it, and the marginal return of the final third is about 0.006.
evidence_quote: We showed the judge none, a random subset (63% of the constraints as realised; see §11) or all of an instruction's constraints, and the loop moves from -0.120 to +0.042 to +0.048 (Figure 17). Most of the gap closes well before the world is complete.
mismatch_note: Same SHAPE as our P3 ceiling (coverage gain saturates) but not the same object or measurement: the partially-shown set is the task's own constraint list handed to the judge, not a generated rubric or a set of authored criteria, and the outcome is repair-loop pass rate, not coverage against a golden rubric. Single sweep on 300 responses; the authors acknowledge the 'half' arm actually showed 63% of the constraints 'in a different representation from the full arm' (paper.md:L586), so a representation confound is not excluded. The 63% subset was random, so the result does not distinguish 'the omitted third was easy' from 'the omitted third was irrelevant'. Direction-only support for an upper bound, not a measurement of one.

venue: arXiv preprint (Hosho; cs.AI/cs.CL; 50 pp.; not peer-reviewed)
their_construct: Criterion-set manipulation inside the same IFEval loop: ask the judge whether the response satisfies EVERY constraint in the instruction instead of whether it is good, i.e. supply a per-task acceptability criterion in place of the generic quality rubric that Table 2 diagnoses as the status quo in a typical LLM judge. Outcomes: net change in pass rate, false-positive rate on satisfied constraints, and number of responses acted on.
their_finding: Stating the per-task goal did not improve the net regulatory outcome (+0.055 against +0.065, interval crossing zero), although it reduced the judge's false-positive rate on satisfied constraints from 0.553 to 0.405 and narrowed the responses acted on from 275 to 228.
evidence_quote: Stating the goal to the judge, by asking whether the response satisfies every constraint in the instruction instead of whether it is good, did not improve the net outcome (+0.055 against +0.065, with an interval crossing zero). It did reduce the judge's false-positive rate on satisfied constraints, from 0.553 to 0.405, and narrowed the set of responses acted on, from 275 to 228.
mismatch_note: The nearest thing in this paper to a rubric-level manipulation, and it is still not ours. The criterion set is GIVEN by the instruction, not generated by an LLM and not compared against an expert golden rubric; and the outcome is net repair gain, not criterion coverage. It is a caution against over-reading P1's practical payoff rather than evidence for or against P1: in these grounded-text tasks the binding constraint was the evidence channel, and making criteria explicit bought precision, not recall or outcome. It does not contradict H1 (which asserts coverage<1, not that coverage buys outcome) and does not threaten P1 novelty; it does mean criterion-set completeness was not the bottleneck in this setting.

their_construct: Rubric WEIGHTING, not coverage. The criterion set R is held fixed and treated as complete; the weight vector w is estimated from the user prompt x and R alone (never from candidate responses) and shared across all candidate responses (arxiv.tex:148, 341). ICW elicits pairwise 'which criterion is more important for this prompt' judgments from an LLM weighting model (GPT-4.1 by default) in both display orders, maps only order-agreed judgments onto an AHP positive reciprocal matrix with a fixed ratio alpha, takes weights from the principal eigenvector, and re-compares all pairs while the consistency ratio CR > tau (arxiv.tex:216-305). Evaluation metric = pairwise preference accuracy against human preference labels on 6 benchmarks (RubricBench, ResearchQA, JudgeBench, RM-Chat, Chat-Hard, Precise-IF; rubrics for the last 4 come from the RubricARM-8B discriminator/generator), plus downstream GRPO RL (arxiv.tex:358-379). No coverage/recall/match/precision/alignment metric to a reference rubric exists anywhere in the paper.
their_finding: Uniform weighting is systematically inferior: it loses to nearly all weighting methods on all six benchmarks (Uniform Acc 0.771 / 0.583 / 0.762 / 0.740 / 0.805 / 0.720) and ICW beats Uniform on every benchmark by 1.64%-5.79% relative, beating every baseline (RubricBench 0.795 vs 0.782 RaR/ChasingTail; ResearchQA 0.612 vs 0.610 RRD-WU; JudgeBench 0.783 vs 0.772 RRD-WU; RM-Chat 0.769 vs 0.760; Chat-Hard 0.818 vs 0.816 RaR; Precise-IF 0.762 vs 0.756 RACE-SC) (arxiv.tex:405-414, 435-437). Direct holistic LLM weighting is weak and unstable (below Uniform on RM-Chat and Chat-Hard, arxiv.tex:406, 430-431); correlation-based downweighting (RRD-WU) is the strongest baseline (arxiv.tex:433). Gains are 0.6-3.1 accuracy points with no significance test, seed spread or CI reported (grep for significan|std|seed|error bar|confidence interval returns nothing).
evidence_quote: ICW consistently outperforms all baselines, improving the accuracy over Uniform by up to 5.79\%.
mismatch_note: Differs at the load-bearing point: the criterion SET is assumed complete and only its weights vary, so the paper says nothing about coverage/completeness/omission vs a golden rubric (P1), nothing about overlap between two independently generated single rubrics (H1(b)), and nothing about multi-rub union/saturation curves (H1(c)). Its 'overlap' is WITHIN-rubric redundancy (several criteria describing the same property, arxiv.tex:164; handled by downweighting correlated criteria, arxiv.tex:433) — not cross-rubric overlap. Relevance to our protocol is a caution plus a tool, not evidence: (i) a plain cardinality coverage metric ignores that criteria are unequally important, so our protocol must state explicitly whether 'coverage' is unweighted criterion coverage (the currency of RubricBench Recall, RubricRAG Missed@0.2, AxisRubric) or importance-weighted coverage; (ii) pairwise-importance + principal eigenvector + CR is a cheap way to elicit weights when a rubric source ships none, and their fair-comparison control ('all methods share the same rubric sets and verification results, and differ only in the weights', arxiv.tex:377) is reusable. But in our setting the LLM is the object under test, so using an LLM weighting model to define golden coverage would be circular; expert weight oracles already exist in our candidate golden sources (HealthBench +/- point values, ResearchRubrics mandatory +/-4/+5; records 2505.08775, 2511.07685).

their_construct: Provenance and validation of criterion weights: who supplies them, and whether they are ever checked against an expert/reference importance standard. Weights come from one LLM weighting model conditioned on prompt+R only; the weights that the rubric sources themselves ship are deliberately deleted so every method re-weights the identical criteria; the only validation signal is downstream agreement with human pairwise preference labels.
their_finding: Criterion weights are never validated against expert/reference importance. The authors strip the source weights ('The weights provided by the rubric sources are removed, so that all methods weight the same criteria for each user prompt.', arxiv.tex:362); expert-specified weights are acknowledged as the existing practice but 'costly and difficult to scale' (arxiv.tex:739); and the LLM weighting model is admitted to lack domain knowledge in specialized domains, with 'Incorporating expert-specified comparisons remains a valuable direction' listed as future work (arxiv.tex:717). No weight-vs-expert correlation, rank agreement or calibration number is reported for the ICW weights (or for the deleted source weights).
evidence_quote: The weights provided by the rubric sources are removed, so that all methods weight the same criteria for each user prompt.
mismatch_note: A provenance/validity caveat for weighted coverage, not evidence for or against P1/H1/H2. It neither checks whether LLM-assigned weights agree with expert importance nor whether the stripped source weights were themselves calibrated (cf. 2604.01375#gt, where 10/48 expert rubrics were anti-calibrated). Consequence for our protocol: if a golden source already carries expert weights, use them; if we elicit weights with an LLM instead, the LLM-vs-expert weight agreement must be reported first, otherwise a 'weighted coverage' number is confounded with the very model family we are testing. It does establish that in this line of work the weight axis is validated only indirectly (downstream preference accuracy), i.e. an importance-weighted coverage metric against an expert oracle is still unmeasured in the corpus read so far — an absence-of-evidence claim over our record set, not a full census.

their_construct: Zero-shot self-recognition of code authorship, no rubric. Five core generators (GPT-5, Claude Haiku 4.5, Gemini 2.5 Flash, Grok 4 Fast, DeepSeek-V3-0324) on MBPP/HumanEval/DS-1000. Task 1a = pairwise 'which of these did you write' over 14 evaluator-opponent cells; Task 1b = single-solution yes/no (one third positives) scored by balanced accuracy plus both yes-rates. Controls: seven non-LLM heuristics (longer/shorter, docstring, type hints, comment count) on the same items, position-balanced accuracy, Holm correction, and a TF-IDF + logistic-regression classifier as an upper bound on the authorship signal present in the code.
their_finding: Zero-shot self-recognition is near chance. Across 14 pairwise cells accuracy correlates r=0.93 with how often the evaluator's own solution is the longer one; the only cell clearly above chance (GPT-5 81.9% vs Grok) is beaten on the identical pairs by the 'choose the longer' rule (97.5%) and by 'choose the docstring' (91.8%). Individual-presentation balanced accuracy is 49.4-58.2% across all 15 model-benchmark cells (only two Grok cells survive Holm), while raw accuracy 38-67% tracks yes-rate policy (GPT-5 never answers yes; Grok/Gemini say yes 58-97% of the time).
evidence_quote: Across the 14 cells, accuracy correlates with the fraction of pairs in which the evaluator's own solution is the longer one at Pearson $r=0.93$, with a slope of 0.54 … On GPT-5's pairs with Grok the rule ``choose the longer solution'' scores 97.5\% and ``choose the solution with a docstring'' 91.8\%, both above GPT-5's own accuracy … Balanced accuracy ranges from 49.4\% to 58.2\% over the 15 combinations
mismatch_note: Different construct: attribution of code authorship. There is no rubric, no criterion set, no golden standard and no coverage measure anywhere in the paper (case-insensitive grep on main.tex for 'rubric', 'criteri', 'coverage' returns zero hits). It constrains only the self-recognition rival, and only in the code domain, where functionality is publicly testable so quality can be held fixed and style can be stripped. It says nothing about whether coverage differences drive bias. Transferable point: a measurable authorship signal can exist in the text while zero-shot judges cannot reach it, so 'the signal exists' and 'the judge uses it' must be measured separately — the same distinction applies to 'the golden rubric contains the aspect' vs 'the model's rubric covers it'.

their_construct: Blind pairwise self-preference on MBPP. The judge sees its own solution and another model's with no authorship information and is asked which is better, explicitly told to disregard comments/docstrings/formatting (prompt at main.tex:L289). For pair X vs Y, both X and Y judge the same items and Delta = P(X chosen|X judges) - P(X chosen|Y judges); a neutral third model Z outside the pair splits Delta into Delta_X and Delta_Y. Rerun on items where both solutions pass or both fail. Then an AST normalization (strip docstrings, comments, type hints; rename local variables/params/nested functions; re-serialize; Pass@1 unchanged item-by-item) re-runs the same judges, and a TF-IDF classifier measures how much authorship signal survives.
their_finding: The only clear original-code self-preference is Claude Haiku vs DeepSeek: Claude's own component +11.8 points (p<1e-3), combined Delta +11.0, unchanged on the quality-matched subset (+11.4 on 228 items). It is a general documentation taste rather than authorship: Claude picks the documented solution 84% of the time when exactly one has a docstring, but also 76% when it judges a third-party pair (Gemini vs DeepSeek), and shows no preference against the also-documented Gemini (-2.7). After normalization no component is significant (Claude's own component -1.1, combined +4.3); the two normalized results that stay significant follow residual length differences. Meanwhile the trained classifier still attributes normalized code at 93-96%, so the judges lost the cue, not the signal.
evidence_quote: the only clear self-preference is Claude Haiku's against DeepSeek: Claude chooses its own solution 75.2\% of the time, while Gemini and DeepSeek, judging the same items, choose Claude's 63.4\% and 64.2\%. Claude's own component is $+11.8$ points ($p<10^{-3}$) and DeepSeek's is near zero, and the combined effect is unchanged on items on which both solutions pass or both fail ($+11.4$ on 228 items). Much of it is a taste for documentation rather than for its own code: on items where exactly one solution has a docstring, Claude picks the documented one 84\% of the time, but as the neutral judge of Gemini vs.\ DeepSeek it also picks the documented solution 76\% of the time … On normalized code no component is significant; Claude's own component falls to $-1.1$ and the combined $\Delta$ against DeepSeek to $+4.3$. To the extent that self-preference exists in this setting, it resides in the same removable surface features as self-recognition. … a simple trained classifier still separates GPT-5's normalized code from other models' code at 93--96\%, while no zero-shot judge does better than 58\% on those pairs. The signal exists in the code; asking a model whether the code is its own does not reach it.
mismatch_note: The sharpest opponent baseline found for H2, but not the same construct: the attribute is removable surface form (docstrings/comments/type hints/local names/line count), not coverage of an expert criterion set; no rubric, no golden-rub, no omission measure. What it does establish is the mechanism SHAPE H2 proposes — a general preference that coincides with one's own generation habits produces apparent self-preference without self-recognition, because the same preference is applied to third-party pairs. Limits: only 4 original pairs, of which 1 is significant; perplexity is cited (wataoka2024selfpreference) but never measured, so this is not a style+perplexity+coverage variance decomposition; the domain is code, where semantics can be normalized. Note also that instruction-level control failed (the prompt told the judge to ignore comments/docstrings/formatting, yet the preference persisted and only structural normalization removed it): H2's confound control must be structural, not verbal.

their_construct: Measurement-validity protocol for self-attribution / self-preference claims: balanced accuracy plus both yes-rates instead of a single accuracy; abstentions/refusals excluded and reported; seven non-LLM heuristic rules scored on the identical items, with the best rule taken as an upper bound on any fixed rule; position rates and position-balanced accuracy; model-name order in the prompt randomized independently of solution order; a label-consistency test when both targets of a pair are judged (same answer for both targets = inconsistent; different answers = consistent, then correct or inverted); strict first-line answer parsing; and a strip-the-confound re-run with a trained classifier as the reference for how much signal remains.
their_finding: A single yes/no accuracy against a 50% baseline is uninterpretable: with 0% vs 97% true-positive policies, raw accuracies of 61-66% and 40% rank response policy, not ability. An earlier prompt that aligned name order with solution order let 8 of 10 runs score 86-99% from the name order alone (two others far below chance, 19.9% and 31.0%). The consistency test turns below-chance aggregate accuracy into evidence of discrimination plus a mislabeled prior: on Opus/Gemini 68.1% of items are consistent-and-inverted vs 7.0% consistent-and-correct.
evidence_quote: A single accuracy for yes/no self-recognition is uninterpretable without the two yes-rates: our data contain a model with a 0\% true-positive rate scoring 61--66\% and one with a 97\% true-positive rate scoring 40\%, so a study that reports one number per model ranks models by their response policy. … An earlier version of our attribution prompt listed the author names in the same order as the solutions, which let most judges score 86--99\% from the name order alone. … on the Opus/Gemini pair the judge does so on 75.1\%, with 68.1\% of all items consistent and inverted against 7.0\% consistent and correct
mismatch_note: Protocol-level rather than construct-level: it prescribes how to keep self-preference measurements free of artifacts, not whether coverage matters. Its pieces transfer directly to H2 — response-bias-aware metrics, heuristic baselines scored on the identical items, prompt-order decoupled from label order, and 'strip the confound structurally then re-measure, keeping a trained classifier as the signal-availability reference'. But its confounds are hand-built surface rules, not rubric criteria, and its signal reference is a classifier rather than an expert rubric; for coverage the analogue would be: after removing surface cues, does the judge's covered-aspect profile still predict its verdicts, and does the golden rubric show criteria the judge never uses?

their_construct: 准则集级的跨模型『交集共识』组装 + 准则级专家盲评。三异质生成器 GPT-5 Mini / Gemini 2.5 Pro / Claude Sonnet 4.5 各自从『问题+参考答』独立提 20–30 条原子准则（提示词要求多角度覆盖并含部分参考答不满足的 stretch goals，Prompts.tex:L22–L39）；DeepSeek-V4-Pro 审核（拒 REJECT / score<8）并按语义聚类；支持集 S_l={g: C^(g)(q)∩G_l≠∅}，仅保留 |S_l|=3 且 reference-coverage 标签一致的簇，每簇取最长成员、按维度配额截断到 ≤10 条内容准则 + 2 条全局控制（5,166 prompt / 49,046 内容准则 / 10,332 全局控制）。专家研究：17 个匹配 RaR-Medicine 题，consensus 面板与单生成器面板同题、同条数(8)、同 reference-coverage 正负构成；双专家盲评 136 准则×2 条件×4 个二元属性（medical validity/atomicity/clinical relevance/non-redundancy），分歧不裁决、按题 cluster bootstrap 95% CI。下游：Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 做 GRPO，Qwen3-32B 做三态判官；4 个准则源（3 单生成器 + consensus）在相同 5,166 prompt、同 seed、同预算、二值打分下比较。
their_finding: 准则级：consensus 面板 clinical relevance 99.3% vs 单生成器 86.8%/86.0%（+12.5/+13.2 pp，95% CI 均不含 0）；medical validity 近天花板（+1.5 pp，CI 碰 0），atomicity 与 non-redundancy 无显著差异且点估计为负（-5.1/-2.9、-2.2/-2.9 pp），『四项全过』+2.9/+5.9 pp 但 CI 均含 0。下游二值消融：consensus 医疗均分 49.26 vs 单生成器 47.51–48.93，HB-Hard 32.71 vs 23.56–26.02；完整方法 HB-Hard 38.98±1.04。作者自陈三生成器可能共享同一错误，且一致同意会排除只被 1–2 个模型提出的有用准则。 The authors also note: the three generators may share the same error, and unanimous support can exclude useful criteria identified by only one or two models.
evidence_quote: Both experts rate 99.3\% of the criteria from the complete construction pipeline as clinically relevant, compared with 86.8\% and 86.0\% for the matched single-generator panels. The corresponding gains are 12.5 and 13.2 percentage points, with 95\% CIs of \([6.6,19.1]\) and \([6.6,20.6]\).
location: papers/2608.10996/ConRubMed2027-ArXiv.tex:L359 (正文结果); 表 papers/2608.10996/ConRubMed2027-Supplementary-Body.tex:L295-L326; 设计 L259-L268 与 L348
mismatch_note: 只支持 P3 的『组装 > max(单rub)』方向，不支持其机制归因。(1) 组装是交集共识（|S|=3 才保留），保留集在集合论上 ⊆ 每个生成器的候选集，因此不可能给出 H1(c) 要的『覆盖率 > max(single)』；本文明证下游增益可以在不扩覆盖（反而缩小集合）时发生 → 是『组装增益 ≠ 互补性』的反例。(2) 整条流水线 = DeepSeek-V4-Pro 审核（拒 REJECT/低分）+ 改写 + 10 条配额；审核环节无消融，单生成器面板是否经过同一审核也未说明，故 +12.5 pp 不能归因于跨模型互补。(3) non-redundancy 点估计略负，即『不同评分靶点』未增加。(4) 专家研究 n=17（24 抽样中 6 题不在最终训练集、1 题不满足 coverage 构成），双专家 κ=0.357–0.573（原始一致率 0.809–0.993），真值噪声中等；下游只跑 1 个训练 seed、无 CI。(5) 准则由『问题+参考答案』条件化生成并复诵同一份多角度清单，模板本身机械抬高跨生成器重合，会系统性低估真实漏集（cf. 2603.11027 的通用维度结构混淆）。(6) 判官 Qwen3-32B 与被训 Qwen3-4B 同族，但全文无任何 self-preference / 风格 / perplexity / 自我识别测量，对 H2 无增量。

their_construct: 作者在 Limitations 对其『一致支持=交集』构造的自陈边界：三生成器可能共享同一错误；一致同意会排除只被 1–2 个模型提出的有用准则。该构造与聚类提示词一致：单模型独有准则被明确排除在任何语义组之外（Prompts.tex:L119），且数据统计只报保留后的『Three-generator support 100%』（Supp:L74）。
their_finding: 作者明确承认 consensus 设计无法保留、也未测量『单模型独有准则』；跨模型被漏准则集合的规模与重合/相关性在其论文中完全不可见。这是对空缺 A 的正面反证（该量尚未被测），而非对 H 的真值证据。
evidence_quote: The three generators may share the same error, and unanimous support can exclude useful criteria identified by only one or two models.
mismatch_note: 这句话是自陈限制，不是测得的效应。与 A 的关系：他们只报保留集（|S|=3）的质量，不报 |S_l|=1/2 的簇数、跨模型 Jaccard/相关、并集覆盖或漏集重合；聚类提示词逐字规定 'Criteria that are unique to one model (no match) should NOT appear in any group'（Prompts.tex:L119），审核还会先删除 REJECT/低分准则，使单模型独有量在论文内不可复原。可做的算术界：每 prompt 3×(20–30)=60–90 候选，最终均值仅 49,046/5,166=9.49 条内容准则（中位数=90 分位=最大值=12 总条数，说明 ≤10 条配额对至少一半 prompt 生效），即 ≥84% 候选被丢弃——但丢弃原因混合了审核拒绝、支持<3、去重与配额截断，不能反推漏集大小。对 H1(b) 最多算『存在单模型独有准则』的弱前提，不构成重合率证据。

their_construct: Ten LLMs (Claude Opus 4.7, Gemini 3.1 Pro, GPT-5.5, Grok 4.3, Qwen3.6-Plus, DeepSeek-V4-Pro, Kimi K2.6, Llama 4 Maverick, Mistral Large 3, Qwen3.6-35B-A3B) act as both selectors and judges. Evaluation targets are sets of 20 narrative constraints chosen from a shared pool of 200 pre-written single sentences (30 runs/model, 300 sets); no generated text, so model-specific surface style is structurally removed while a source signature remains recoverable (leave-one-out k-NN source-model accuracy 50.7% vs 10% chance; within-model Jaccard above a random null). Judges score every selection on a FIXED, exogenously given 4-dimension rubric (Originality, Dimensionality, Coherence, Tellability; 7-point Likert), 3 reps: Exp1 = 10 judges x 300 selections x 3 = 9,000 blind runs. Primary statistic is a mixed-effects coefficient beta_S: score = b0 + bS*is_self + (1|judge) + (1|selector) + (1|selection_id), random intercepts absorbing judge severity, selection quality, and repeated-selection non-independence, reported per rubric dimension. Exp2 = quality-matched self/other pairs (within 0.25 overall and 1 point per dimension; 40 pairs/judge) in a 2x2 label x actual design with ANONYMOUS labels ('your own selection' / 'another language model'), 4,800 runs, model score = b0 + bL*label + bA*actual + bLA*(label x actual) + (1|judge) + (1|selection_id). No perplexity/log-probability covariate and no self-recognition probe were run; familiarity is argued, not measured.
their_finding: Raw self-other gaps exist in BOTH directions (7/10 judges rate own selections higher: Kimi K2.6 +1.09, GPT-5.5 +0.86, Claude Opus 4.7 +0.51; Grok 4.3 -0.67, Qwen3.6-35B-A3B -0.90). With all 10 judges, beta_S is positive for Avg (+0.181), Dimensionality (+0.316), Coherence (+0.276), Tellability (+0.278) and negative for Originality (-0.144). After excluding the two low-discrimination judges (Llama 4 Maverick, Mistral Large 3, both placing >=81% of ratings on two adjacent scores), every positive effect vanishes (Avg +0.003 [-0.05,0.06]; Dim +0.039; Coh +0.042; Tel +0.065, all n.s.), leaving only a negative Originality effect (-0.133 [-0.21,-0.05]) that runs opposite to self-preference and is not robust to a random-slope specification (tau = 0.41-0.63). Experiment 2 shows a label main effect bL > 0 on every dimension (Avg +0.43, Org +0.53, Dim +0.57, Coh +0.29, Tel +0.32, all p<.001) with bA and bLA non-significant everywhere, i.e. the displayed attribution label alone shifts scores of identical, quality-matched targets, bidirectionally (6 symmetric self-inflation+other-deflation, 2 self-boost, 1 other-penalty, 1 general-penalty). Authors conclude apparent self-preference here is a measurement artifact (selection quality + judge severity), familiarity does not drive it, and authorship attribution is a distinct driver.
evidence_quote: After excluding the two, all positive effects disappear; only the negative \textit{Originality} effect remains, which is contrary to self-preference.
mismatch_note: Closest rival account and strictest baseline, but NOT a test of H2's coverage mechanism. (1) The rubric is exogenous and identical for all judges: 'By directing each judge to assess specific, theoretically grounded properties rather than self-selecting which aspects to attend to' (3_Methodology.tex:L41). Criterion coverage is therefore held constant by construction; the paper never measures which criteria a judge covers, nor any per-judge/self-generated criterion set, so the H2 predictor (coverage) has zero variance by design and the null beta_S is compatible with H2 rather than contrary to it. (2) 'Familiarity thus does not appear to be a substantial driver' is an inference from the design, not a perplexity measurement; no NLL/log-probability covariate was computed (0 hits for 'perplexity' outside Related Work/Discussion prose). (3) Self-recognition is not instrumented: the k-NN result shows a recoverable signature (50.7%), and the authors concede the signal 'may be too weak for a judge to recognize its own selections' (5_Discussion.tex:L10). (4) One creative task (plus a research-proposal replication with anchored 1-10 scales), no human-validated rubric (7_Appendix.tex:L90), anonymous labels rather than real model names. Consequence: supplies the per-dimension decomposition template and the mandatory controls, but leaves gap B open. H2 must add a coverage predictor to this exact model and show incremental R^2 over per-dimension beta_S with selector-quality and judge-severity random intercepts, AND control the label/authorship channel (bL-type) that this paper proves is independently sufficient.

their_construct: The 4-dimension evaluation rubric (Originality, Dimensionality, Coherence, Tellability; anchors at 1 and 7) is used as a fixed comparative instrument across conditions. Originality and Coherence are adapted from the Torrance Test of Creative Writing with anchors rewritten to selection-level material; Dimensionality is a newly introduced selection-level construct; Tellability follows Labov/narrative theory. Scoring is direct absolute scoring (not pairwise) precisely so a single rating can be moved by the label manipulation.
their_finding: The authors explicitly did NOT validate the rubric against human annotation, and state it functions only as a held-constant comparative frame for condition differences, not as an absolute quality measure; validating against human judgments would be required before using it to score quality in absolute terms.
evidence_quote: We did not validate the rubric against human annotation. It functions as a held-constant comparative frame, since our claims concern differences in how a fixed instrument is applied across conditions, not absolute quality scores.
mismatch_note: Their rubric is an unvalidated, researcher-authored, held-constant instrument - it cannot be used as golden-rub ground truth, and their paper makes no claim to criterion completeness or expert agreement. For our golden-rub construct this is a negative example: a fixed 4-dimension frame is adequate for within-condition comparisons but has no external truth anchor. Also relevant: because the same instrument is imposed on every judge, criterion-level coverage differences are definitionally absent, so a null self-preference here says nothing about a golden-rub coverage gap.

their_construct: Pairwise LLM-judge win rates on 500-example samples of AlpacaEval (helpfulness), WMT19 de-en (helpfulness) and TruthfulQA (truthfulness); judges = Llama-3.1-8B/70B, Qwen2.5-7B/72B, gemma-2-9B in both base and Instruct/it form; gold judgment = average verdict of three strong LLMs (GPT-4o-mini, Gemini-1.5-Flash, DeepSeek-V3) deliberately taken from model families different from the tested judges to avoid preference leakage; DBG score = judge's win rate for its own responses minus the gold win rate; temperature 0, response order swapped and averaged, maximum response length constrained to suppress length bias.
their_finding: Naive self-minus-other scoring overstates self-preference when the judge's own answers are genuinely better: with Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct as judge its own-response score is 52.3%, above Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct's 50.0%, yet still below the gold judgment's 54.5%, so the apparent bias is quality. DBG removes this confound and still finds positive bias: Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct 41.7% vs Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct 2.1%, Llama-3.1-8B 21.6% vs Llama-3.1-70B 0.4%, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct 0.2% vs its 25.6% pre-trained counterpart. Bias exists before post-training and is smaller in larger models.
evidence_quote: Since gold judgments reflect true response quality, the DBG score mitigates the confounding effect of response quality on bias measurement.
mismatch_note: Not a coverage study: case-insensitive grep of the full source for rubric/criteri/coverage/dimension returns zero hits, and there is no criterion set, no missed-aspect variable and no expert rubric. Its 'true quality' is an LLM-consensus pairwise win rate, so DBG is a difference against an opinion aggregate, not against a golden rubric; the estimator also assumes a weak correlation between the quality gap delta and bias b_A (L203), and validity rests on a 100-item human check (74% agreement). The unit is the response, not the criterion, so the residual cannot be attributed to any evaluated aspect. Value for H2 is instrumental only: it supplies a dependent variable whose quality confound is reduced, not evidence that criterion coverage explains extra variance.

their_construct: Intervention on surface style: DeepSeek-V3 rewrites both models' responses into 'attractive' and 'humorous' styles (DeepSeek-V3 is then removed from the gold-judge pool); DBG is recomputed before vs after the rewrite; semantic preservation of the rewrite is checked with gte-multilingual-base [CLS] embeddings plus t-SNE.
their_finding: Unifying surface style reduces but never eliminates DBG: Llama-3.1-70B 3.3% to 1.4% and Llama-3.1-8B 18.7% to 7.2% under the attractive rewrite; Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct 2.0% to 1.2% and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct 8.4% to 5.9% under the humorous rewrite. The authors therefore conclude that response content beyond style also contributes to self-preference.
evidence_quote: Furthermore, we note that style modifications alone do not entirely eliminate the model self-preference phenomenon, suggesting that the content of the responses may also contribute to self-preference bias.
mismatch_note: This is the cleanest existing before/after template for H2's residual claim, but the residual is only named 'content' and is never operationalized: no criterion set, no measured predictor, no regression, no R^2 or delta-R^2 (grep for regress/R^2/variance/residual over the full source returns zero hits), only DBG point estimates before and after a manipulation. So it demonstrates that a style family leaves variance on the table without quantifying the unexplained share or showing that any coverage variable can absorb it. Its style manipulation is register-level (attractive/humorous), not the full style/perplexity/self-recognition family that H2 must control. Methodological hygiene worth copying: the rewriter was excluded from the gold-judge pool to avoid leakage.

their_construct: Fine-tune Llama-3.1-8B and Qwen2.5-7B on identical data (UltraChat-200k) with identical settings, then compare DBG against their standard Instruct versions and against Instruct models trained on different data and methods; judge pairs are evaluated on AlpacaEval.
their_finding: Training two different models on the same data reduces DBG (Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct 10.5% to 2.1%, Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct 2.1% to 1.1%), while differently-trained Instruct models show larger scores (6.1% and 7.6%). A residual persists after same-data training, which the authors read as generation-evaluation discrepancies laid down in pre-training surviving into fine-tuned models.
evidence_quote: Moreover, even after further training on the same dataset, the two models continue to exhibit self-preference bias, suggesting that discrepancies between response generation and evaluation established during pre-training may persist and influence the behavior of downstream fine-tuned models.
mismatch_note: This is the closest published articulation of H2's 'generation and evaluation cover the same subset' idea, but the shared thing is the post-training corpus, not a criterion set: the authors infer generation-evaluation discrepancies from a DBG change and never measure generation or evaluation content, let alone criteria. No rubric and no coverage variable anywhere in the paper. Consequence for positioning: a reviewer who knows this sentence can read H2 as a restatement of it, so H2 must be worded specifically as coverage of a golden criterion set (and must beat shared-data/provenance as an explanation), not merely as 'generation and evaluation share a tendency'. It does not threaten H2's construct-level novelty, since the construct was not measured, but it does constrain the wording.

their_construct: Gold judgment = mean pairwise preference of three strong LLMs (GPT-4o-mini, Gemini-1.5-Flash, DeepSeek-V3) whose families differ from every tested judge; validated against human pairwise annotations on 100 randomly sampled AlpacaEval instructions comparing Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct vs Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct responses.
their_finding: The LLM-consensus gold reproduces the human pairwise picture closely: gold win rate for Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct is 66% vs 63% from humans, and gold and human annotations agree on 74% of the 100 sampled pairs.
evidence_quote: On the $100$ samples, the human-annotated win rate for Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct is $63\%$, whereas the gold judgment indicate a win rate of $66\%$. More specifically, we find that human annotations and gold judgment results agree on $74\%$ of the samples.
mismatch_note: The gold is a pairwise quality aggregate, not a criterion-level expert rubric, so it cannot license any statement about which criteria were covered or missed; it is a usable template only for the validation step (human subsample vs gold proxy). Precision is limited: 74% agreement on n=100 is roughly +/-9 percentage points at 95% confidence, and only 100 of the 500 instructions were checked, so the check establishes rank-level plausibility, not criterion-level truth. Also note the leakage control (gold judges drawn from other families) as a protocol detail our golden-rub design should adopt.

venue: ACL ARR 2026 October Submission (under review, private)
their_construct: Causal label x definition cross-pairing: pair each rubric dimension's label with another dimension's definition while holding the item and judge fixed; 8 judges ranging Gemma 3 270M up to two frontier models; SummEval and DialSummEval (HelpSteer2 a descriptive third corpus); outcomes are score/label-vs-definition attribution, agreement with human ratings, best-of-N pick value, plus linear probes / logit lens inside Gemma 3 27B. (All reconstructed from the abstract only.)
their_finding: Abstract reports: contrary to the authors' hypothesis, the score follows the definition rather than the label, yet agreement with human ratings changes little; removing or replacing the definition lowers agreement slightly for Gemma judges and more for frontier judges; scrambling the definition changes many best-of-N picks while the human-rated value of picks barely changes; inside Gemma 3 27B the definition is read in the middle layers and item ranking follows a shared quality signal that linear probes can decode before the rubric is read.
evidence_quote: Inside Gemma 3 27B, the definition is read in the middle layers, and the ranking of items follows a shared quality signal that linear probes can decode before the rubric is read. A rubric edit that moves the scores is therefore no evidence of better measurement.
location: OpenReview API v2 note content.abstract (forum bNSVlDItzb), retrieved via api2.openreview.net/notes/search; Tier-0, no full text (no file:line available)
mismatch_note: TIER-0 ONLY - must not be used as evidence. Full text is inaccessible: OpenReview forum/PDF/attachment return 403 to both anonymous and authenticated browser user ('User Kewen Qiu does not have permission to see Note bNSVlDItzb'), the hashed PDF URL returns 404, no arXiv mirror exists (searched by title and by abstract phrases), no author copy found via WebSearch, no Wayback snapshot, and the paper-search OpenReview reader reports 'OpenReview denied anonymous access; private/authenticated content is not supported'. Construct mismatch: their manipulation swaps label vs definition inside a FIXED rubric vocabulary; it never varies WHICH criteria a rubric covers, never measures omission against a golden-rub criterion set, and never assembles multi-model rubrics. So it cannot speak to H1(a)/(b)/(c). For H2 it only proposes a competing internal mechanism (a shared pre-rubric item-quality signal) but has no coverage-difference variable, so it mandates a control variable, not a refutation. relation_to_H is therefore provisional and marked low confidence.

their_construct: Rubric-conditioned pairwise judge given ONE synthesized criterion. The DV is the 'stubbornness rate' S: the share of judgments on which the judge, after being shown a rubric that favors the response it did NOT pick rubric-free, still keeps its prior-chosen response. Four open-weight judges (gemma-4-12B, gemma-4-31B, Qwen3.6-27B, Qwen3.6-35B-A3B) x four preference datasets (UltraFeedback, HelpSteer3, RewardBench-reasoning, RM-Bench); both presentation orders averaged, ties disallowed. Confidence c = log p(y_p) - log p(ȳ_p) read at the verdict token WITHOUT any rubric. Rubrics are generated by gpt-5.6-luna with m=1 criterion each; RubricBench expert rubrics are used only as a held-out transfer test for the tuned instruction.
their_finding: When a rubric contradicts the judge's own (rubric-free) preference, the judge keeps its own verdict on 6.2-23.6% of judgments across the 4x4 grid (10.4-14.9% UltraFeedback, 6.2-8.0% HelpSteer3, 19.8-23.6% RewardBench, 15.0-20.2% RM-Bench); on the two open-ended datasets the judgments it keeps have higher pre-rubric confidence for all four judges. RubricLens (GEPA tuning of the judge instruction only, no weight change) raises flipped-rubric agreement from 86.2% to 92.6% on average and lowers S to at most 13.9%, and it transfers to expert-written RubricBench rubrics without re-tuning. The authors warn that agreement under the ORIGINAL rubric is saturated (0.959-1.000) and cannot demonstrate rubric-following, because the prior may already pick that response.
evidence_quote: When the rubric conflicts with its prior, the judge keeps its own choice on 6–24% of judgments before tuning and still on 3–14% after (Table 2).
mismatch_note: Not P1(b)'s construct, and not close to it. (1) Unit is the whole verdict, not a criterion set: the paper explicitly limits itself to 'single-criterion rubrics' (Limitations, paper.md:L241) and Appendix F uses 'm = 1 criterion per rubric' (paper.md:L353). With one criterion per rubric there is no way to measure which criteria are used vs ignored, and no missed-criterion set exists. (2) Cross-model comparison is only of aggregate S per judge x dataset; item-level overlap of the pairs each judge ignores is never computed, and no phi/Jaccard/co-occurrence is reported. The only cross-model statement is a qualitative suspicion in Appendix D: 'model families fail on different pairs, and an instruction tuned on one judge's failures fixes mainly those' (paper.md:L339), with no measurement. (3) The conflicting rubric is adversarially synthesized by gpt-5.6-luna to favor one response; it is not an expert golden rubric and there is no coverage-vs-ground-truth metric. (4) Different object: they measure the judge's adherence to a GIVEN rubric, whereas P1(b) is about the GENERATED artifact's coverage of a golden rubric. Hence this is not P1(b)'s nearest construct; P1(b) (cross-model missed-set overlap) remains unmeasured. Separately useful as a measurement-validity caution: original-rubric agreement is saturated (0.959-1.000) and the authors state high agreement 'does not reflect the judge's rubric-following ability' (paper.md:L241), so an agreement-based coverage metric must exclude this regime.

their_construct: 条件规则下的 judge 行为研究：8 个 open-weight judge（Gemma-4 12B/26B-A4B/31B、Qwen3.5 9B/27B/35B-A3B、Qwen3 32B、OLMo-3.1 32B；9–35B，无 reasoning，greedy）对同一 response 评一套规则，规则有 4 种写法（R0 无例外 / RW 仅豁免 / RI 例外内联替代义务 / RS 独立规则），数据为 SafePyramid（300 triples + 299 held-out）与用 ProfBench/HealthBench 专家/医生标注准则拼出的规则（response 与标签固定，只改 rule text）。DV=P('violated') on the waived rule；base-rule evidence e=其余 7 个 judge 对 waived rule alone 的 margin 均值；dependence=β_RW vs β_R0，share kept=margin 比；obligation spillover=DiD τ；95% cluster bootstrap。无 golden-rubric 覆盖率度量。
their_finding: 判定并不按 rubric 忽略被豁免的证据：条件成立时（正确判定为 not violated），P(violated) 仍随 base-rule evidence 上升（最强三分位 .18–.55），YES–NO margin 保留无例外时 21–54% 的 dependence（slope .07/.16/.21），且只替换被豁免的 criterion、response 固定即可复现（δ=.13 ProfBench、.18 HealthBench）；在 judge 单独答对被豁免规则与条件的条目上仍发生。第二类失败：失败的 replacement obligation 会计入被豁免规则（τ=.31/.16/.13），把它写成独立规则可大部分消除（.23/.15/.10）。
evidence_quote: Once the exception applies, whether and how strongly the response violates the waived rule should not matter, but it does.

venue: arXiv preprint (IAENG journal template; arXiv API/abs page shows no journal_ref and no comment)
their_construct: 3x4 label-manipulation on blog posts. ChatGPT-4o, Gemini 2.5 Flash and Claude Sonnet 4 each write one ~200-word blog per each of 10 titles (30 posts); all three then evaluate every post, its own included, under four attribution conditions: no label / true label / false-label permutation A (GPT-as-Gemini, Gemini-as-Claude, Claude-as-GPT) / permutation B (GPT-as-Claude, Gemini-as-GPT, Claude-as-Gemini). Two outcomes: percentage-based 'best' preference votes, and 0-10 point ratings on a FIXED three-dimension form (Coherence, Informativeness, Conciseness) converted to percentages. No coverage/omission metric, no golden rubric, no variance decomposition - the effect is read off per-condition bar charts.
their_finding: Explicit model-name attribution moves evaluations a lot while content is held fixed: the 'Claude' label raised scores and the 'Gemini' label depressed them across all three evaluators, and false attribution reversed preference rankings (up to 50 pp on preference votes, <=12 pp on rubric ratings). Content identical, label swapped: Gemini awarded 60.7% to a ChatGPT-authored post labelled Claude; Claude's own content mislabelled Gemini fell -28.2 pp, while Claude's true-label self-preference rose +13.3 pp. Inside the fixed three-dimension form, informativeness was the most label-sensitive dimension and conciseness the most stable, which the authors read as 'structural qualities may be evaluated more objectively than perceived informational value'. No statistical tests, CIs or variance decomposition are reported anywhere.
evidence_quote: Three consistent trends emerged across conditions. First, the "Claude" label acted as a strong positive bias cue, while the "Gemini" label consistently triggered negative bias. Second, false labels reversed rankings in overall preference scores (swings up to 50 percentage points), whereas point-based ratings showed smaller but aligned shifts (<=12 percentage points).
location: papers/2508.21164/IAENG_LaTeX_pub.tex:L553 (N=10 titles x 3 models = 30 posts); L557 (four label conditions, two scoring systems, fixed 3-dimension form); L639 (content-fixed false-label reversal, 60.7% ChatGPT-as-Claude); L641 (Claude +13.3 / -28.2); L643 (three trends, 50 pp / <=12 pp, informativeness vs conciseness)
mismatch_note: Construct mismatch is large. The word 'rubric' never occurs in the full text (grep -c 'rubric' = 0), as do 'coverage', 'perplexity', 'golden' and 'expert' - the fixed 3-dimension Coherence/Informativeness/Conciseness form is held constant across all four conditionss, so there is no criterion set that can be omitted, no golden-rub ground truth, no single-vs-multi rubric comparison, and hence nothing that can speak to H1(a)/(b)/(c), P1-P3, or questions A/C. For B (coverage difference as an SPF mechanism) the paper has no coverage variable at all and reports no regression/R^2, so it cannot supply the 'extra variance' measurement H2 requires; it supplies only a rival channel: an explicit name/brand prior that is not in our opponent list (style / perplexity / self-recognition / author fingerprint). Note the channel is not self-recognition proper - the effect is trans-model and asymmetric (all evaluators penalise the 'Gemini' label even when the text is not Gemini's), i.e. a learned reputation prior about the label, not detection of one's own output. Evidence quality is weak: 30 documents, 10 titles per evaluator, preference expressed as a percentage of 10 votes (so a '50 pp swing' is a 5-vote change), figure-only reporting, no CIs, no significance tests, no released data, no peer-reviewed venue. Its implied label-channel magnitude also conflicts with the rubric-based identity-reveal contrast in record 2611.18616#ctl, where revealing model identity shifted verdicts by only ~8% of the blinded bias. Therefore: a control variable and a hypothesis-generator, not a refutation, not an anchor.

venue: ICLR 2026 (accepted); arXiv:2502.01534 v3 2026-03-04 camera-ready LaTeX source read
their_construct: 维度级分析：用 GPT-4o 把 judge 的 rationale 中提到的每个 aspect 归入 AlignBench 的 9 个固定维度（Factuality、User Satisfaction、Logical Coherence、Richness、Creativity、Fairness and Responsibility、Completeness、Clarity、Others），再按维度计算 PLS。
their_finding: 报告主观维度（如 fairness）泄漏高于客观维度（如 completeness）；但同一段末句写成 'preference leakage tends to be more significant in objective questions and dimensions'，与前句直接矛盾。
evidence_quote: This observation is also applied to judgment dimension analysis, as objective dimensions (like completeness) have an overall lower leakage degree compared with subjective ones (like fairness). This suggests that preference leakage tends to be more significant in objective questions and dimensions, where the contaminated model is more likely to receive biased preference.
mismatch_note: 这不是准则级覆盖：维度标签是对 judge rationale 的事后归类，输入是 judge 自己写的理由，不是 model 生成的准则集合，也没有 golden-rub。它最多说明偏差集中在主观质量侧面（与覆盖机制可共存的背景），不能作为覆盖证据。段落内部自相矛盾（objective lower vs more significant in objective），该组结果不宜引用，confidence 降为 med。

their_construct: Pairwise LLM-as-judge on verifiable benchmarks with gold answers (MATH500, MMLU, MBPP+). Every self-preference event is labelled by truth: legitimately justified when the judge's own response is the correct one, harmful when the other model's response is correct. Metrics: SPR (self-preference ratio), LSPR (share of self-preferences that are correct), HSPP (rate of preferring one's own incorrect response when the other response is correct). 11 judges (Qwen2.5 3B-72B, Llama-3.x 3B-70B, Gemma-2 9B/27B) against a fixed 7-model evaluatee pool; position bias controlled by evaluating each pair twice with swapped order.
their_finding: Self-preference can be objectively split by ground-truth correctness into a legitimate and a harmful component; the split is a decomposition of preference events, not of variance.
evidence_quote: This enables us to distinguish \emph{harmful} self-preference (favoring objectively worse responses) from \emph{legitimate} self-preference (favoring genuinely superior ones).
mismatch_note: No rubric and no criteria set anywhere (verified: 0 occurrences of 'rubric' in the LaTeX sources). Ground truth is a single answer-correctness bit, so 'legitimate' means 'the judge's own answer matches the gold answer' — there is no analogue for multi-criterion golden-rubric coverage in this design. It also measures only exact-self preference (judge's own output vs another model), not same-family or style-similar preference.

their_construct: LSPR = (over the D_diff subset where exactly one of the two responses is correct) the share of self-preferences in which the judge's own response is the correct one. LSPR is then correlated at the model level with task accuracy across the 11 judges.
their_finding: For the strongest models the overwhelming majority of self-preference on MATH500 is ground-truth-justified — Qwen-2.5-70B 96.57% and Llama-3-70B 95.16% — with 80.98%-88.78% on MBPP+ and MMLU; LSPR rises with capability.
evidence_quote: In particular, Qwen-2.5-70B and Llama-3-70B achieve LSPR of 96.57$\%$ and 95.16$\%$ on MATH500, respectively.
mismatch_note: These are model-level aggregates over a fixed evaluatee pool, and the accompanying correlations are across ~11 model points (caption: 'Each circle represents one LLM', tex/3-corre.tex:L9), i.e. ecological correlations, not item-level variance explained. The paper never reports R^2 or a residual-variance statistic (0 occurrences of 'variance' in the sources; the only 'R^2' is a commented-out footnote at tex/3-corre.tex:L54). It supplies the quality-explained baseline H2 must beat, not a measurement H2 can copy.

their_construct: HSPP = on D_diff instances where the judge's own response is incorrect and the other model's response is correct, the probability that the judge still prefers its own response; reported per model and correlated with task accuracy.
their_finding: A substantial residual harmful self-preference survives on the judge's own-error instances, and it is largest for the most capable judges: Qwen2.5-72B reaches HSPP 86% on MATH500 and 73% on MMLU, above its overall SPR of 55% and 52%.
evidence_quote: Notably, the most performant model, Qwen2.5-72B, exhibits an HSPP of 86$\%$ on MATH500 and 73$\%$ on MMLU, significantly higher than its overall SPR (\Cref{fig:corre_task_acc_sp_ratio}) of 55$\%$ and 52$\%$, respectively.
mismatch_note: This residual is conditioned only on the binary stratum 'own answer wrong / other right', not on which criteria the judge failed to apply; no style, perplexity or self-recognition covariate is entered, so HSPP is an unconditional residual rather than additional variance. The authors' own explanation is error-recognition — 'This suggests stronger models struggle more to recognize when they are wrong' (tex/0-abs.tex:L15) — a capability account adjacent to self-recognition, one of H2's named opponents. Useful as the magnitude H2 must explain beyond truth, but it is not a rubric-coverage measurement.

their_construct: Style/quality disentangling by subset contrast: SPR is recomputed on D_diff (exactly one response correct, so correctness decides) versus D_agree (both responses correct or both incorrect, where the authors assume preference reflects style/formatting); a capability-matched evaluator-evaluatee replication is added in the appendix.
their_finding: The D_diff SPR curve is steeper and sits above D_agree for strong models, which the authors read as self-preference being grounded in objective correctness rather than style; no regression adjustment and no variance decomposition is performed.
evidence_quote: on $\mathcal{D}_{\text{agree}}$, the preference is driven primarily by style or formatting.
mismatch_note: The 'style' control is a stratum label, not a measurement: no style, length or perplexity feature is extracted, and D_agree pools both-correct with both-incorrect items (two different ambiguity regimes). The borrowable pattern for H2 is item-level matching on golden-rubric satisfaction (measure residual self-preference where ground truth is tied), not a regression residual. A drafted oracle-gap metric delta_oracle = |SPR_oracle - SPR_evaluator| exists but is commented out in the source (tex/3-corre.tex:L135-L147) and is not a reported result.

venue: arXiv (cs.AI; ICLR 2026 模板，无正式发表 venue)
their_construct: 42 tasks / 7 domains。把偏好分解为 P(X)=V(可执行程序)+A(LLM 判分的 rubric bank)+T(只有稠密模型才有的部分)+ε；所谓“覆盖”并非对专家 rubric 的覆盖率，而是 articulated share =(AUC(VA)−.5)/(AUC(VAT)−.5)，即自动挖掘并优化的 rubric bank 相对稠密全模型所恢复的可判别偏好信号的占比。标签是 found behavioral judgments（Reddit upvotes / accept-reject / prize / citation），没有任何专家撰写的 golden rubric（main.tex:536）；rubric bank 由多模型 proposer 池（Claude Opus/Sonnet、gpt-5.6、GLM-5.2）提案后合并审计而成（main.tex:931）。
their_finding: 每个领域都存在 articulability/verifiability gap：code、math、journalism、law ≥85% 的偏好可被 articulable 准则覆盖，humor/creative writing/peer review 只有 61–85%；creative writing 与 peer review 的 gap 占 shared preference 的 34–39%；verifiable 程序只解释 13–80% 的 shared preference。
evidence_quote: While ${\ge}85\%$ of preference in code, math, journalism and law can be articulated; only $61$--$85\%$ can in humor, creative writing and peer review (Figure \ref{fig:cover-photo}).
location: main.tex:L148（同段落 L143 给出 gap 定义；L338 给出 34–39% 量级）
mismatch_note: 他们的“覆盖”分母是行为标签的可判别性、上限是稠密模型 VAT，而不是专家 golden-rub 的准则集合；他们没有做 single-rub 对专家准则的逐条覆盖，也没有跨 LLM rubric 作者的漏集重合检验。因此这构成“准则级覆盖不完备已经是可量化对象”的先例（这正是 P1 测量部分的新颖性风险），但不是 H1(a) 的直接证据；且其 bank 已是多模型组装，未做单 backbone vs 多 backbone 的受控对比。
