their_construct: 多 proposer 准则 bank 的 head-to-head：把 4 个外部准则发现方法（HypoGeniC、HypotheSAEs、ExperiGen、RL-XAR 风格 rubric meta-optimization）与自有 74 条 bank 各自拟合，再构造 union / ours+union；committed articulated ceiling = max(ours, ours∪ext) + Good–Turing whisker；在 13 个有共享评测框的任务上比 held-out AUC，稠密模型为参照上限。多样性轴是“发现算法”，外部方法共享同一个 Qwen3-32B（main.tex:965）。
their_finding: 没有任何 articulable 模型（包括把全部 bank 堆叠起来）在任何任务上追平稠密全模型；union 相对自有 bank 的实现增益在 10/13 任务上超过 whisker，故 ceiling 取 union；但 union 并不稳定优于最佳单 bank（自有 bank+whisker 对最佳外部 bank 5 胜 8 负）；13 个 bounded 任务的 tacit share 对自有 bank 平均 .38、对 committed ceiling 平均 .21。单任务上 8 条准则的 RL-XAR bank 达 .678，74 条 bank .689，稠密模型 .743（joke upvotes），说明准则数量带来的收益很快饱和。
evidence_quote: Second, the union's realized increment over our bank exceeds our campaign's whisker on ten of thirteen tasks, which is why the committed ceiling stacks the union on our bank rather than relying on the whisker alone.
location: main.tex:L1505（数值见 main.tex:L1475 与 Table tab:metric-discovery, main.tex:L1490-1500）
mismatch_note: 组装轴是准则发现算法（且共享同一 judge 模型），不是我们定义的“多 LLM/多视角 rubric”；结果是 bank 级预测 AUC，不是准则级覆盖率；union>best-single 也不稳定成立。因此它只在 P3“准则并集存在上限、需要 ceiling”这一论断的形态上构成先例，不是 P2/P3 的直接测验；且无 golden-rub 参照，无法回答“多 rub 对专家准则覆盖率的增益”。

venue: arXiv (cs.AI; ICLR 2026 模板，无正式发表 venue)
their_construct: 用 capture-recapture / Good–Turing 估计“未被任何 proposer 提出的准则”的价值：把准则视为 species，μ=q(U) 为 missing mass，μ̂=f1/N（最后一轮提案中首次出现 species 的比例）；whisker=G·μ̂/(1−μ̂) 是从提案计数推出的未挖掘价值上界（G 为已实现增益）。多 proposer 扩展用各家族互相“重捕”的重叠模式估计 μ∪；以 fresh proposal fleet、round-ahead backtest、leave-one-proposer-family-out recovery 校验 mass 估计，以 30 个截断点 backtest 校验 value 映射；rare-event 用 k* 反演“要推翻结论需多大的一个漏网准则”。
their_finding: 该 bound 在 30 个截断点中 18 个成立（限 k≥3 时 13/16），并在 mid-campaign 之后有较大余量；据此判定 press pickup、BBC most-read、spotlight picks、#HashtagWars 四个 campaign 不需要任何未发现准则即可达到全模型。多 proposer 的 μ∪ 只给出构造与 LOO 校验，论文报告的数值 ceiling 用的是单 sampler whisker 加 union 的实现增量，并未报告 μ∪ 的点估计。
evidence_quote: Discoveries pool into $D = \bigcup_j D_j$, and the missing mass of the mixture, $\mu_{\cup}$, is estimated from the overlap pattern between families in the capture--recapture manner \citep{chao1984nonparametric, boehme2018stads}: how often family $j$ rediscovers what family $j'$ already found measures how much of the space each family misses.
location: main.tex:L1193（推导 L1163-1200；backtest L1215-1370；单轮 μ̂ 与 whisker 表 L1290-1310）
mismatch_note: 这是“未被任何 rubric 覆盖的准则可被估计规模/价值”的可测化装置，正是 A/C 测量部分的核心需求；但 (i) 无 golden-rub，value 是相对行为标签的 AUC 边际而非准则覆盖率；(ii) 多 proposer μ∪ 只到设计+LOO 验证，未报告数值，不能算作已完成跨模型漏集重叠测量；(iii) 依赖 salience-ordered mining 与次可加上界，迁移到“每条 rubric 的准则集合”需逐项重验。它使“首个把覆盖不完备做成可界定量”这一新颖性主张失效，但不测 A 的跨模型漏集重合，也不测 B。

their_construct: Cross-model behavioral-dependence audit on objectively verifiable answers. 18 LLMs from 6 families (GPT/Claude/Qwen/Llama/Gemini/DeepSeek), MMLU-Pro split into two disjoint 1,000-question subsets (bio 473 + psych 527 for dependence estimation; law 295 + business 705 for judge-bias evaluation). For models i,j and task t, Y_{m,t} in {0,1} is the binary ERROR indicator. Conditioning variable: task difficulty d_t = failure rate of the OTHER M-2 models (leave-pair-out, so the tested pair cannot enter its own conditioner); task easiness a_t = 1 - d_t. Null H0: Y_i,t independent of Y_j,t given d_t; each model's marginal failure probability is modelled by a logistic difficulty-response function p_m(d). Level 1 BEI_w(i,j) = (1/T) sum_t a_t^w (Y_i,t Y_j,t - p_i,t p_j,t), i.e. easiness-weighted excess co-failure. Level 2 CIG(i,j) = (1/T) sum_{t: Y_i=Y_j=1} (-log c_t)(Z^dir - c_t), where c_t = sum_k pi_{k,t}^2 is the null same-distractor collision probability from a smoothed task-specific distractor distribution estimated from the other models (leave-pair-out). Inference: one-sided Monte-Carlo null (resample both models' binary outcomes from fitted marginals, keep observed d_t, recompute the statistic) plus Benjamini-Hochberg FDR across all model pairs. Baselines: Pearson correlation, mutual information, co-failure Jaccard of failure sets, error-only answer agreement, IRT-style difficulty-adjusted residual correlation.
their_finding: After BH-FDR correction, significant pairwise BEI and CIG form a behavioral-dependence graph; strongest edges are intra-family (e.g. Llama-3-70B / Llama-3.1-70B BEI=0.0525, q=9.5e-4) plus cross-family and cross-generation pairs (GPT-5 / Claude-4.6-Sonnet CIG=0.0471, q=1.09e-3). The easiness weighting is substantive: weight exponent w=0 (unweighted mean co-failure residual) gives Spearman rho with judge over-endorsement of 0.289 on MMLU-Pro and 0.032 on MATH-500, versus 0.508/0.441 at w=1 and 0.490/0.275 at w=2. Raw co-failure Jaccard is a significant but weaker and non-transferring baseline (rho=0.428, p=0.012 on MMLU-Pro; 0.275, p=0.175 on MATH-500). Entanglement-aware verifier reweighting gives 0.882 accuracy vs 0.847 majority vote (+3.5 pp).
evidence_quote: We define the null hypothesis as behavioral independence conditional on task difficulty. Intuitively, among tasks of the same difficulty, the correctness outcomes of two models are assumed to be independent: once task difficulty is known, observing whether one model succeeds or fails provides no additional information about the other model's outcome.
mismatch_note: Object-level mismatch, not a hit on A/B/C. (1) It measures whether ANSWERS are wrong (MMLU-Pro / MATH-500 objective correctness), never whether RUBRIC CRITERIA are covered: no LLM-generated rubric, no expert golden rubric, no coverage/missed-set indicator. The only 'rubric' in the paper is the fixed 2-item scoring template shown to judges (correctness 0/1 at L1042-1043, reasoning quality 0-5 at L1068-1078) and it is never an object of analysis. (2) The conditioner maps structurally but not literally: their d_t = failure rate of the other M-2 models; our analog would be criterion c's 'catchability' = share of the other k-2 rubric generators that include c. Both control for marginal prevalence, so the null design transfers, but with k=3 generators the leave-pair-out d_c collapses to a single 0/1 indicator and no logistic difficulty-response curve can be fitted; k>=5-6 (or a latent-trait / pooled-bin calibration) is needed. (3) BEI/CIG are pairwise only: no k-way union, no saturation ceiling, so nothing here for P3. (4) The evidence is association, not causal: the authors say the audit 'identifies behavioral association but does not establish its causal origin' (L756).

their_construct: Judge over-endorsement measured as a target-conditional precision drop: DeltaPrec(J_j, M_i) = P(Y=1 | Yhat_j=1) - P(Y=1 | Yhat_j=1, M=M_i), where Y=1 means the target-model response is ground-truth correct and Yhat_j=1 means judge J_j endorses it. Positive DeltaPrec = the judge's precision on that specific target model is below its overall precision (more over-endorsement). Three judges (Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct, GPT-5, GPT-4o-mini) under a joint cross-evaluation prompt, response order shuffled; each judge scores correctness (0/1) and reasoning quality (0-5) using a fixed rubric. Entanglement BEI/CIG for each (judge, target) pair is estimated on a DISJOINT MMLU-Pro subset and correlated with DeltaPrec across pairs via Spearman; transfer test on MATH-500 with 14 available models. Joint-prompt vs independent-prompt ablation on 500 questions finds no significant DeltaPrec shift (paired t, p=0.421) and rank-equivalence (p=7.6e-5).
their_finding: On the disjoint MMLU-Pro subset, rho(DeltaPrec, BEI)=0.508 and rho(DeltaPrec, CIG)=0.520 (p<0.01); on MATH-500, 0.441 and 0.457 (p<0.05). Pearson correlation and mutual information are weak/non-significant; error-only agreement and IRT residual correlation are non-significant; raw co-failure Jaccard is significant on MMLU-Pro (0.428, p=0.012) but not on MATH-500 (0.275, p=0.175). The authors read this as structured failure-based dependence capturing judge-target coupling that aggregate similarity misses.
evidence_quote: On MMLU-Pro, BEI and CIG show the strongest associations with $\Delta\mathrm{Prec}$, with Spearman coefficients of $0.508$ and $0.520$, respectively ($p<0.01$).
mismatch_note: NOT self-preference and NOT coverage. (1) The protocol states 'Each model is required to evaluate the performance of all other models under a unified cross-evaluation protocol' (L963), and no self condition is reported anywhere; the (judge, target) pairs are therefore related/other models, and DeltaPrec is over-endorsement of a TARGET MODEL's correctness, not preference for the judge's own answer. It is evidence for the authors' 'related-model / entangled-model favoritism' line, not for H2's self-preference. (2) The judge-facing rubric is fixed and never analyzed, so 'coverage of the golden rubric' has zero variance by construction; shared style/family similarity and shared error structure cannot be separated. (3) Inference is a pair-level Spearman across roughly 3 judges x 18 targets (~51 pairs, minus self pairs), an ecological correlation with no variance decomposition; there is no nested-regression DeltaR^2 and no control for style, perplexity, self-recognition, or author label. (4) The DV uses ground-truth Y=1 conditioning, which is a useful design ingredient, but it is not an SPF measure.

their_construct: Contrast of two ways to build the negative half of a judge-bias item: (a) LLM-generated negatives (oracle-less) vs (b) mechanical perturbation of a gold answer ('gold-labeling by degradation', oracle-bearing, e.g. entity/number/negation swap). Positive control: 50 Turkish wiki40b sentences with numerals, first numeral replaced; a 30%-Bernoulli silent no-op is injected (seed 42, 20 realized no-ops), so some emitted negatives are identical to their gold. Oracle = gold-to-negative string comparison. Task is binary factual-vs-hallucinated faithfulness; judges are DeepSeek-V4-Flash, gemini-3.5-flash, glm-5.2; 17,800 cached calls.
their_finding: The string-comparison oracle separated all genuine perturbations from all injected no-ops (50/50) with zero API calls and zero human reading, while the same fault class in the oracle-less design had escaped four aggregate robustness checks (larger N, replication, a converging mechanistic account, a controlled producer-swap) and was found only by manually reading raw generations.
evidence_quote: This is the same class of failure (a silent degeneration producing a useless negative) in a design that does carry an oracle. The oracle, a gold-to-negative string comparison, flagged every no-op and confirmed every genuine perturbation, at 50/50 accuracy, with zero API calls, zero human reading, and O(N) cost. The same fault class that required four rounds of robustness checking plus a manual read to surface in our oracle-less design was caught mechanically and instantly here.
mismatch_note: Zero occurrences of 'rubric' or 'criteri*' in the source; the ground truth is item integrity on a binary factual-vs-hallucinated task, never an expert criterion set. They put criterion-style coverage explicitly on another axis: 'Those are real limitations, on a different axis (naturalness and coverage of the negative space) than the one we isolate (whether item integrity is mechanically checkable).' (L945-L948). They also disclaim preference/quality settings outright: 'the entire measurement operates on a binary faithfulness classification, factual-versus-hallucinated; how a generation fault of this class propagates into preference or quality-comparison judgments, where there is no correct reference answer to compare against, is a genuinely different question and one this paper does not address.' (L1131-L1136). So the device can verify that a constructed control item is what it claims to be (a genuine violation), but not that a golden rubric is correct. Borrowing it also imports its own limitation: a rule-built negative 'can be distributionally unnatural, can cover only the perturbation types its authors implemented' (L943-L945), which would narrow the criterion-violation space our coverage estimate is measured on.

their_construct: A pre-aggregation stimulus-validity rule for oracle-less generation designs: for every distinct generation condition (each producer, language and prompt template), manually read 15-20 raw generated items in full before computing any statistic. Sample size is derived from n >= ln(1-C)/ln(1-p) for confidence C at fault rate p.
their_finding: At C=99%, n=7 suffices at a 50% fault rate, n=13 at 30%, n=21 at 20%, n=44 at 10%; they adopt 30% as a conservative reference (their own fault ran at 100%) and set 15 as the floor and 20 as a margin. They state the numeric thresholds come from this single case and only the diagnostic shape is claimed to generalize.
evidence_quote: Read. Manually read fifteen to twenty raw generated items in full. The two endpoints are the two ends of one calculation, not two independent arguments. The sample size needed to see at least one faulty item with confidence C at fault rate p is n >= ln(1-C)/ln(1-p), which for C=99% gives n=7 at a 50% rate, n=13 at 30%, n=21 at 20%, and n=44 at 10%.
mismatch_note: The rule is stated per 'generation condition' of an LLM-generated stimulus field, i.e. it presupposes that a generation step produced the items. If our single-rub/multi-rub conditions are LLM-generated rubric outputs, the same gate applies directly to the rubric text; if the items are expert-written, the fault class it targets (silent truncation/degeneration of a generated negative) does not exist and the gate degenerates into ordinary quality review. The authors themselves flag non-universality at L1021-L1034: the values 'are not universal ... we offer them as a worked example, not a calibrated standard.'

their_construct: Two mechanical, zero-API degeneration metrics reported per generation condition alongside every aggregate result: (i) fraction of items whose generated field is identical to its source field; (ii) fraction that begin with a conversational opener or are a fragment shorter than three words. A companion step reports the mean word count of the generated field and treats a length far from what the prompt asked for as the first mechanical flag (L1006-L1010).
their_finding: In the corrupted DeepSeek/Turkish condition 12.2% of items were verbatim repeats of the factual field and 81.0% began with a truncated conversational opener; mean generated length was roughly 2 words against 20-47 words in the corrected/other conditions, and generation validity went 0.0% -> 98.8% after the budget fix.
evidence_quote: Measure degeneration. Report two rates: the fraction of items whose generated field is identical to its source factual field, and the fraction that begin with a conversational opener or consist of a fragment shorter than three words. In our fault these were 12.2% and 81.0% respectively; either, reported alongside a result, tells a reader whether the items the statistics summarize were well-formed at all.
mismatch_note: Both rates assume a source/factual field to diff against; a golden rubric has no single gold string, so they would have to be re-derived per criterion (e.g. an expected-span overlap or criterion-satisfaction-string check) rather than copied. The device's value for us is as a reporting obligation before coverage numbers are aggregated, not as a coverage measure: it detects that the stimuli are malformed, and says explicitly it 'is not designed to detect judge bias itself' (L1038-L1041).

their_construct: Stratifies each judge's Markdown-bullet style score by the word length of the factual field, across three conditions: corrupted DeepSeek-produced Turkish (mean 2.1 words), unaffected Gemini-produced Turkish (mean 43), and English HaluEval (mean 2.2), with two-proportion tests (DeepSeek z~8.7, GLM z~7.0).
their_finding: Judge style preferences are stable signatures, but their magnitude, and for DeepSeek their sign, track stimulus length: DeepSeek goes 0.24 (1-2-word EN) / 0.43 (1-2-word TR) to 0.81 (16+-word TR), crossing 0.5; GLM 0.90/0.89 to 0.65; Gemini flat at 0.00. The apparent cross-lingual invariance was a length invariance misread as a language invariance.
evidence_quote: First, the style preferences are not invented: each judge carries a signature that no length condition erases (Gemini plain throughout, GLM Markdown throughout). Second, their magnitude, and for DeepSeek their direction across the 0.5 line, is a function of how much text the style marker was attached to, which is a property of the generation pipeline, not of the judge.
mismatch_note: This is a confound-control device, not a coverage result: the outcome is a binary formatting preference, not criterion coverage, and no rubric exists. What transfers is the requirement to length-stratify any aggregate metric compared across conditions, because a metric can change sign across length regimes (DeepSeek 0.24 -> 0.81). Two secondary cautions for our golden-rub: their English reference set (HaluEval, mean 2.2 words) sat in the same length regime as the corrupted data, and they admit they 'did not re-audit its individual items' because of its reputation (L753-L770, L1138-L1156) - reputational trust of an external benchmark is itself the oracle-less trap, so an expert-annotated golden set we adopt must still have its item-level properties reported.

their_construct: Two artifacts of the same stimulus fault, both initially read as real judge effects: (i) a controlled producer-swap experiment (Gemini instead of DeepSeek produces the hallucinated negatives, judges and task fixed), which looked like a producer-judge interaction; (ii) a within-producer factual-accuracy deficit, briefly read as a self-reference effect.
their_finding: Both dissolved after the decoding budget was separated: GLM's selection accuracy on DeepSeek-produced items went 0.61 -> 1.00, and DeepSeek's within-producer factual accuracy 0.88 -> 1.00; no cross-lingual, producer-specific, or self-referential effect survived. Producer-swap is listed by the authors as one of four robustness checks that made the fabricated effect more convincing rather than exposing it (L1183-L1185).
evidence_quote: DeepSeek's apparent within-producer deficit, factual accuracy 0.88 on its own generations, which we had briefly entertained as a self-reference effect, resolved to 1.00 under the same correction. No cross-lingual, producer-specific, or self-referential effect survived.
mismatch_note: Directly relevant as a validity caution for H2, not as evidence about it: the self-preference candidate here is a producer-equals-judge factual-accuracy deficit on a binary task, not rubric-conditioned self-preference, and it was exactly zero after the stimulus fix. It does not measure coverage -> SPF variance and cannot support or threaten H2's mechanism; it only shows that a self-referential effect can be manufactured by degenerate stimuli, so any H2 residual (delta_oracle-style or otherwise) must be computed after an item-integrity gate. It also demonstrates a negative methodological fact: producer-swap and within-producer accuracy are not sufficient validity controls, because a broken stimulus can make both point the wrong way.
